note: Places where the most animals found nowhere else live (after Myers et al., 2000, and later hotspot lists), with a few animals to look for in each; and common animal names for the search box. Positions are centres; radius in km.
hotspots: Cut off for about 88 million years: every lemur on Earth lives here and nowhere else.
Volcanic islands about 1,000 km off Ecuador whose finches and tortoises helped Darwin explain evolution.
No native land mammals except bats, so birds took their place, and many of them cannot fly.
The most isolated island chain on Earth: nearly all its native land birds live nowhere else.
A fragment of the old southern continent with its own birds, geckos and conifers.
One of the oldest rainforests on Earth, home of orangutans and proboscis monkeys.
The only forest where tigers, rhinos, elephants and orangutans live side by side.
More than 7,000 islands, many with birds and mammals of their own.
On Wallace's Line, where Asian and Australian animals meet; many of its mammals live nowhere else.
The largest tropical island: birds-of-paradise, tree kangaroos and egg-laying mammals.
Ancient rainforests and eucalyptus woods with marsupials and the egg-laying platypus.
Walled off by desert and sea: thousands of plants and several marsupials live only here.
The last wild stronghold of the Tasmanian devil.
Mountains older than the Himalayas, with rainforest frogs, monkeys and goats found nowhere else.
An island with its own monkeys and birds, and many frogs and lizards found nowhere else.
Volcanoes and cloud forest that are the only home of mountain gorillas.
The roof of Africa, where Ethiopian wolves and geladas live and nowhere else.
The smallest of the world's six floral kingdoms, with birds and antelopes found only here.
The richest hotspot on Earth, from cloud forest to high grassland.
Only about an eighth of this coastal forest is left, home of the golden lion tamarin.
A land bridge between two continents, crowded with birds, frogs and cats.
The largest Caribbean island, home of the smallest bird in the world.
Islands from snow to subtropics: its snow monkeys are the most northerly monkeys on Earth.
Bamboo forests that are the only wild home of the giant panda.
Remote ranges where the saola, a forest ox, was discovered only in 1992.
Between the Black and Caspian Seas: wild goats and grouse found only on these peaks.
Home of the Iberian lynx and the Barbary macaque, the only monkey north of the Sahara.
The oldest and deepest lake on Earth, with the only seal species that lives in fresh water alone.
More fish species than any other lake, most of them cichlids found nowhere else.
Granite islands in the Indian Ocean whose birds were brought back from the brink.
The dodo's island: its pink pigeon and kestrel were saved from a handful of birds.
Temperate rainforest cut off by the Andes and the desert, home of the pudú, one of the smallest deer.
Between desert and ocean, with the California condor and foxes found only on its islands.
Penguins and seals that live only around the frozen continent.
Isolated for millions of years: dragon's blood trees and birds and reptiles found only here.
Volcanic islands off Africa with giant lizards and a blue finch found nowhere else.
